title: RecallGuard
description: An iOS app that watches FDA food and pet-food recalls and alerts you only when one reaches your household. Users set the allergens they track and build a pantry by typing items, scanning barcodes, or photographing a grocery receipt; recalls are matched against that pantry and delivered on a severity tier so a labeling technicality never wakes you at 2am. Built end to end — ingestion pipeline, matching engine, receipt parsing, push delivery, and subscription handling.
shortDescription: FDA recall alerts filtered to your allergens, your pantry, and your pets — not everyone else's.
techstack: React Native via Expo with TypeScript, Supabase for Postgres, auth, and edge functions, direct APNs for push delivery, Claude Haiku Vision for receipt line-item extraction, and RevenueCat for subscriptions.

title: Fishing Game Addition in Covey.Town
description: This project involved integrating an interactive Fishing Game Area into the pre-existing codebase, enhancing virtual exploration with engaging gameplay. In this feature, users are able to fish for rare catches, customize avatars, and compete for the highest score on a global leaderboard.
shortDescription: Integrated an interactive Fishing Game into Covey.Town — fish for rare catches, customize avatars, and compete on a global leaderboard.
techstack: Built using TypeScript, React, and Chakra UI, with real-time leaderboard updates via MongoDB. Sprites crafted with Photoshop, optimized using TexturePacker, and deployed via Netlify with automated testing.

title: Determining Bias in the Michelin Guide
description: Analyzed Michelin Guide biases in geographic and cuisine trends using machine learning. Results suggested a preference for established cuisines and high-end restaurants, potentially overlooking more diverse options for one-star ratings.
techstack: Built with Python using pandas, numpy, and scikit-learn. Visualizations were created with matplotlib and seaborn, and predictions were generated with K-NN, Random Forest, and SVM algorithms. Data was sourced from Kaggle.

title: Weekly Routine
description:
A mobile-first PWA for planning a week: meals with macro tracking, workouts, supplements, and a mix of fixed time blocks and flexible tasks. It ran without an account and synced across devices once you signed in.

Most of the work went into the parts nobody sees. Offline-first meant the service worker had to hand off cleanly on update, which took explicitly activating the waiting worker before reload rather than trusting the reload to do it. A global banner surfaced offline and sync-error states instead of letting writes fail quietly. Sign-out got its own timeout so a dead network could not hang the app. Installed iOS PWAs also leave a viewport gap at the bottom that never appears in a browser tab, which took a while to isolate.

I no longer use it. I built it to help me stick to a routine, and routines change quickly. Once I had the hang of mine and it actually held, the app was not necessary anymore. It stays here as a project, not a product.
shortDescription: A mobile-first PWA for planning a week: meals with macro tracking, workouts, supplements, and a mix of fixed time blocks and flexible tasks. Offline-first, so it ran with no account and synced once you signed in. Most of the work was invisible: service-worker handoff on update, a banner surfacing offline and sync errors instead of failing quietly, and an iOS viewport bug that only appears once the app is installed. I built it to help a routine stick. Once mine stuck, it was not necessary anymore.
techstack: Built with TypeScript and React using Vite, styled with Tailwind CSS, backed by Supabase for auth and data sync, and Zustand for client-side state management.
